facts.evidence: Revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026, was $60,801 million, an increase of 28% year-over-year.
Diluted earnings per share (EPS) was $6.18, down 13% from $7.14 in the prior year period.
FoA income from operations was $23,394 million, down from $24,971 million in the prior year period.
The operating margin was 31%, compared to 43% in the second quarter of 2025.
For the third quarter of 2026, total revenue is expected to be in the range of $61–64 billion.
Total costs and expenses were $42,026 million, an increase of 55% year-over-year.
This figure includes $2.40 billion in charges related to legal proceedings and $1.18 billion in severance expenses associated with the May 2026 headcount reduction.
Cash flow from operating activities was $31.86 billion for the quarter. Free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $784 million.
Full year 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, are anticipated to be in the range of $130–145 billion, narrowed from the prior outlook of $125–145 billion.
Family daily active people (DAP) averaged 3.60 billion in June 2026, a 3% year-over-year increase.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue grew 28% to $60.8 billion.
Net income declined 14% to $15.8 billion.
The net income decline was due to the 55% surge in costs and expenses.
claims.note: Causal attribution not made in the release. The release reports costs +55% and net income -14% but assigns no cause; net income was also affected by a higher effective tax rate (16% vs. 11%) and interest and other expense, net of $(19)M vs. $93M income.

claims.claim: Revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $60,801 million, an increase of 28% year-over-year.
On a constant currency basis (non-GAAP), revenue would have increased 27% year-over-year.
Net income was $15,848 million, a decrease of 14% year-over-year.
Diluted EPS was $6.18, down 13% from $7.14 in the prior year period.
Income from operations was $18,775 million, a decrease of 8% year-over-year.
Operating margin was 31%, compared to 43% in the second quarter of 2025.
Total costs and expenses were $42,026 million, an increase of 55% year-over-year.
Costs and expenses include $2.40 billion in charges related to legal proceedings.
Costs and expenses include $1.18 billion in severance expenses associated with the May 2026 headcount reduction.
Family of Apps revenue was $60,370 million for the quarter.
Reality Labs revenue was $431 million for the quarter.
FoA income from operations was $23,394 million, down from $24,971 million in the prior year period.
Reality Labs recorded an operating loss of $4,619 million, compared to a loss of $4,530 million in the prior year period.
Family daily active people averaged 3.60 billion in June 2026, a 3% year-over-year increase.
Ad impressions increased 14% year-over-year.
Average price per ad increased 12% year-over-year.
Third quarter 2026 total revenue is expected in the range of $61–64 billion.
The revenue guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth.
Full year 2026 total expenses are now expected in the range of $165–169 billion.
The full year expense range incorporates the $2.4 billion in legal charges recognized in the second quarter.
Full year 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, are anticipated to be $130–145 billion, narrowed from the prior outlook of $125–145 billion.
Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $90.26 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Long-term debt was $83.66 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Cash flow from operating activities was $31.86 billion for the quarter.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $784 million.
Dividend and dividend equivalent payments were $1.35 billion for the quarter.
The release notes youth-related trials are scheduled for this year in the U.S., which may ultimately result in a material loss.
Headcount was 75,472 as of June 30, 2026, a 1% decrease year-over-year.
Approximately 8,000 employees impacted by the May 2026 reduction will no longer be reflected in headcount by the end of the third quarter of 2026.
claims.note: Overstates the release, which says the ~8,000 impacted employees are included in reported headcount and 'the majority of whom' — not all — will no longer be reflected by the end of Q3 2026.

claims.claim: The company expects its tax rate for the remaining quarters of 2026 to be between 15–17%, an increase from the prior outlook of 13–16%, absent changes to the tax landscape.
